sections.content:
Now it's clear! Clicking the green plus at (19,24):
- The dark gray selection ring moved from the first plus (17-22,16-21) to the second plus (17-22,22-27). So the selection ring follows the clicked green plus (toggle/selection).
- The gray 'g' ring at (18-21,29-32) disappeared (reverted to 'w').
- A new gray 'g' ring appeared at (18-21,11-14) — the 2nd cell of the row (columns 11-14).
So each green plus, when clicked, displays a gray plus outline at a specific "target" cell:
- Green plus #1 (columns 17-20, row 2) → target outline at columns 29-32 (4th cell of the row).
- Green plus #2 (columns 23-26, row 2) → target outline at columns 11-14 (2nd cell of the row).
Interesting! So the mapping is: plus at cell index i (0-indexed within the row) → target at some other index. Row 2 cells: columns 11-14 (idx0), 17-20 (idx1), 23-26 (idx2), 29-32 (idx3), 35-38 (idx4), 41-44 (idx5), 47-50 (idx6).
Green pluses in row 2: idx1 (columns 17-20), idx2 (columns 23-26), idx4 (columns 35-38).
- idx1 → idx3
- idx2 → idx0
- idx4 → ? (not yet clicked; probably idx? )
This looks like a "matching" puzzle: each green plus corresponds to an empty cell where it should be moved. The gray outline indicates the destination. The goal is probably to move all the green pluses to their destination cells (the ones indicated by the outline). Then the board is "solved" — all pluses are in the outlined positions?
Wait, but actually the outline might be the "hole" that the plus should fill. When the plus is at the destination, the outline disappears and the plus sits there.
How do you move a plus? Maybe: click the plus to select it, then use arrow keys to move it? But the arrow keys didn't move anything earlier… but at that time nothing was selected! The arrow keys might move the selected plus!
Let me test: currently the 2nd plus (idx2) is selected (dark ring). Press RIGHT or LEFT and see if the plus moves.
Actually wait — the arrow keys might move the selected plus one cell at a time. Let me test RIGHT.
